findings.title: Javadoc for requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() says "Returns true" but they are void and throw
findings.body: `requireView()` (lines 95-98) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (lines 100-103) are documented as "Returns {@code true} if canView()/canViewClientScopes() returns true". Both methods are `void` and throw ForbiddenException when the check fails. Every other `require*` method in this same interface is documented correctly as "Throws ForbiddenException if ...". These two should be fixed to match.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle the Clients resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` special-cases only `USERS` ("All users" for the type resource, the username for a per-user resource). For a policy whose resourceType is `Clients`, it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Per-client resources are created in `getOrCreateResource` via `resourceStore.create(server, name, owner)` with no display name, and their name is the client's internal UUID. So the "all clients" resource and each per-client resource resolve to a null or opaque name when permissions are rendered. Clients need the same handling: "All clients" for the type resource and the clientId for a specific client.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission uses findByType and returns resource names that are not necessarily client ids
findings.body: `getClientsWithPermission` iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` and adds `resource.getName()` to the result. In `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`, per-client resources are created without a type, so they are not returned by `findByType`. The only resource with type `Clients` is the all-clients resource, whose name is the literal string "Clients", not a client id. If an all-clients permission grants the scope, the result is {"Clients"}, which matches no client. Clients granted individually are never returned. Callers that use this set to filter clients will get wrong results. Either the lookup must also cover per-client resources (and resolve names to client ids), or the method needs an all-clients expansion.

findings.title: Up to five full policy evaluations per client in canView(client) when listing
findings.body: `canView(client)` calls `canView()` (one evaluation on the all-clients resource), then `canConfigure(client)`. That calls `canManage(client)` (a second evaluation) and a CONFIGURE `hasPermission` (a third). Finally it calls `hasPermission(client, VIEW)` (a fourth). Each `hasPermission` does a resource lookup, possibly a policy-store lookup, and a full `evaluatePermission` over all of the resource's scopes. Only one scope is inspected afterwards. When listing clients this runs per client, so cost grows quickly with realm size. Evaluating once and checking several scopes, or passing only the requested scope to the evaluation, would avoid the repetition.

findings.title: Possible NPE: getResourceTypeResource can return null and is passed to findByResource
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(...)` returns null when the schema is not supported for the server (for example admin permissions disabled on the realm while the client still exists) or when the type resource is not found. The result is passed straight into `findByResource(server, resource)` and later dereferenced via `resource.getScopes()`, with no null check. That would turn a permission check into a 500 instead of a plain "false".

findings.title: canView() ignores an all-clients MANAGE grant while canView(ClientScopeModel) honours it
findings.body: `canView()` is `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(VIEW)`. An admin with only the all-clients MANAGE scope therefore fails `canView()`/`requireView()`. `canView(ClientScopeModel)` explicitly accepts `VIEW || MANAGE`, and `canView(ClientModel)` accepts manage indirectly through `canConfigure`. For users, the tests treat manage as implying view. Endpoints guarded by the no-arg `canView()`/`requireView()` will behave differently from per-client and client-scope checks for the same admin.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports left in ClientPermissionsV2
findings.body: The private `getEvaluationContext(...)` is never called. The `logger` field and the imports `Scope` and `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` are also unused. This looks like leftover scaffolding copied from the V1 class (including the token-exchange `kc.client.id` attribute), and it is misleading because V2 throws UnsupportedOperationException for token exchange. It should be removed.

findings.title: Event listener is now gated on V1 feature, so V2 gets no cleanup when a client is removed
findings.body: The whole listener body is now wrapped in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`. This avoids calling the V2 `setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws UnsupportedOperationException. As a side effect, under V2 nothing reacts to `ClientRemovedEvent`. The per-client resource (named after the client UUID) and any scope permissions that reference it remain in the admin-permissions authorization store after the client is deleted. Stale resources and permissions accumulate and show up when permissions are listed. The change also silently drops the previous behaviour in realms where neither feature is enabled. A V2-specific cleanup handler is needed rather than just disabling the listener.

findings.title: Test regenerates the secret of the client used to authenticate the admin client and mutates shared state without restoring it
findings.body: `realmAdminClient` authenticates with client `myclient` and secret `mysecret`. `testConfigureOnlyOneClient` calls `clientResource.generateNewSecret()` on that same client. Once the secret is rotated, any later token acquisition or refresh by this admin client in the class (the token expires, or another test builds a new session) fails with 401 using the old secret. This makes the suite order- and timing-dependent. Other tests also leave persistent changes: they rename `myclient` and `realmClient`, move a default client scope to optional, and create roles on `myclient`. `onAfter` only removes permissions, so these mutations leak into subsequent tests.

findings.title: No coverage for several new V2 client paths
findings.body: The new tests cover manage, configure, view and map-roles(+composite) on clients. There is no test for `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`. Nothing checks that a client with a CONFIGURE or VIEW permission still cannot be managed or modified beyond what is intended. `getClientsWithPermission` and the client-scope management permissions (`canManageClientScopes`, `canView(ClientScopeModel)`) are not exercised either. The `getClientsWithPermission` path is the one with the likely defects noted above, and a test would have exposed them.
